# GEO report: acme-mugs **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 24–33/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 5.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 24. High = (5.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 33. Your `robots.txt` tells every crawler to stay away from the whole site. The pages are also built in the browser, so the HTML a crawler receives is empty. The one unknown is the canonical link (the tag that names a page's main address). I can't tell what it should say without knowing your domain. The scoring cap of 40 doesn't change anything here, because both numbers are already below it. These are results read from code, not measured on a live site. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking all crawlers in robots.txt - **Why it matters:** `Disallow: /` asks search engines and AI search tools not to read any page, so nothing else you fix will be seen. This covers GEO-009 and GEO-014 (6 points lost). - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:2` - **What the code says:** `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 50–59. If the block was deliberate, for example while the site is in development, tell me and I'll adjust this. ### 2. Put the page content in the HTML the server sends - **Why it matters:** many crawlers don't run JavaScript. They see only an empty `
`, so "Handmade ceramic mugs" and the catalogue are invisible to them (GEO-003, 3 points lost). The catalogue is also loaded in the browser after the page opens. - **Where:** `index.html:8` and `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:6` - **What the code says:** `
` and `fetch('/api/mugs').then((r) => r.json()).then(setItems);` - **Size:** Large (prerender the pages at build time, or move to a server-rendering framework) - **Score after this:** 37–46 on its own. Combined with item 1: 63–72. ### 3. Give the pages a real title, description and language - **Why it matters:** every page currently shares the generic title "Vite App", has no description, and doesn't declare a language (GEO-012, 2 points lost). - **Where:** `index.html:2` and `index.html:5` - **What the code says:** `` and `Vite App` - **Size:** Small (a per-page title and description needs a head helper such as `react-helmet-async`) - **Score after this:** 33–41 on its own. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`: plain text, valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers are allowed as intended | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:2`, whole site blocked (assumed goal: be found, no config) | | GEO-014 | Linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:2`, blocks Googlebot and Bingbot on both routes | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical per page | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical tag and no declared domain | | GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `index.html:8`, both routes | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap is discoverable | Problem | Not run | No sitemap, no `Sitemap:` line | | GEO-012 | Title, description and lang are present | Problem | Not run | `index.html:2`, `index.html:5`, no description | | GEO-016 | Pages are reachable through real links | Problem | Not run | `src/main.jsx:11`, 0 of 1 non-home route | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions | Clear | Not run | No `nosnippet`, `max-snippet:0` or headers config in the repo | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Problem | Not run | `src/pages/Home.jsx:5` (Home is a problem, Catalogue is clear: 1 of 2 routes) | | GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | Not run | No mobile app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present | | GEO-102 | App structured data (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app | ## Other problems found - `src/main.jsx:11`: ``. The only way to reach the catalogue is a script-driven button. Replace it with `Catalogue`. This is the cause of the GEO-016 problem above. - `src/pages/Home.jsx:5`: ``. The image has no `alt` text. Add a short description, for example `alt="Handmade ceramic mugs"`. ## Worth considering - **Give each mug its own page:** `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:11`: `{items.map((m) =>

{m.name}

)}`. Mugs are plain text with no links. A page and address per mug would let people and machines land on a specific product. It could also carry price and availability labels (structured data). - **Back up the shipping claim:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:6`: `Thrown by hand in Bristol and shipped worldwide.` Visitors will likely ask about shipping costs, delivery times and returns, and no page answers that in text. - **Add a viewport tag:** `index.html:4`: ``. There's no `viewport` meta tag, so phones may render the page badly. - **Link onward from Home:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:6`: `Thrown by hand in Bristol and shipped worldwide.` The home page has no link to the catalogue in its content. Only the nav button leads there. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015 (canonical):** no domain is declared. Tell me your site's address and I'll mark this Clear or Problem. Once there's a domain, I can also work out the sitemap and canonical tags. - **GEO-003 (server HTML):** if your host prerenders pages outside this repo, the result could change. A live scan would confirm what crawlers actually receive. - **Catalogue contents:** `/api/mugs` is loaded at runtime, so I can't tell what it returns or how many mugs there are. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs `, which compares real crawler visits against their published addresses. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site. There's no `geo.config.json`, so I assumed that. - Both routes (`/` and `/catalogue`) are public and meant to be found. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
